The disease is characterized by aortic dissections at larger diameters than observed in Marfan syndrome.
Aortic arch enlargement is the most consistent cardiovascular finding.

stem: Most commonly, ischaemic mitral regurgitation is due to chronic left ventricle (LV) remodelling following myocardial infarction. The resulting papillary muscle displacement leads to tethering of the mitral valve leaflets and mitral regurgitation. Which one of the following statements regarding ischaemic mitral regurgitation is correct?
options: The presence of ischemic mitral regurgitation following myocardial infarction is associated with a 5-year mortality in excess of 60%.
5-year survival is superior for patients who undergo repair of mitral valve in chronic ischemic mitral regurgitation compared to mitral valve replacement.
Chordal cutting increases the incidence of late recurrent mitral regurgitation and negatively impacts postoperative left ventricular function.
An end-diastolic dimension more than 45 mm is associated with poor reverse remodeling following coronary artery bypass grafting even in the presence of viable myocardium.
Tenting height more than 2.5 mm on echocardiography is a predictor of recurrent regurgitation following repair.

stem: The Arterial Revascularisation Trial (ART) is a randomized comparison of bilateral internal mammary artery (BIMA) versus single internal mammary artery (SIMA) grafting in coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery and is one of the largest randomized trials of surgery ever conducted. Which one of the following statements regarding ART is correct?
options: There was a statistically significant decrease in 30-day mortality after off-pump CABG compared to on-pump CABG.
There was a significant increase in stroke rates after 1 year in the on-pump CABG group compared to off-pump CABG group.
There was a statistically significant increase in the need for intra-aortic balloon pump and renal support after on-pump CABG.
A similar average number of grafts were performed with on- and off-pump surgery.
Repeat revascularisation was significantly higher in off-pump patients at 30 days and at 1 year.

stem: A 50 year old woman with a history of coronary artery spasm and obstructive coronary artery disease underwent coronary artery bypass grafting for unstable angina. Two hours postoperatively she develops marked S-T segment elevation accompanied by hypotension (70/40 mmHg). Initial treatment should include infusion of
The occurrence of postoperative coronary artery spasm following coronary revascularisation is highest in patients with
options: a grafted left anterior descending coronary artery with proximal disease.
a grafted right coronary artery with proximal disease.
an ungrafted (normal) left anterior descending coronary artery.

stem: A 65-year-old man with normal preoperative left ventricular function has just returned to the intensive care unit following coronary artery bypass grafting. His intraoperative course was unremarkable. His initial haemodynamic and laboratory data includes: Pulse: 75 beats per minute Pulmonary artery pressure: 35/17 mmHg Haemoglobin: 11 gm/dL Pulmonary artery wedge pressure: 13 mmHg Blood pressure: 130/84 mmHg Cardiac index: 1.7 L/[min*m2] Systemic vascular resistance index: 4100 dynes sec cm-5/m2 The most appropriate initial treatment of this patient is
options: 250 cc fluid bolus for volume expansion.

stem: A 70 kg man is in the intensive care unit following uncomplicated coronary artery bypass grafting. His ventilator is set as follows: Tidal volume: 1,000 cc Intermittent mandatory ventilation: 12 breaths per minute FiO2: 0.80 Positive end-expiratory pressure: 8 cm H2O Peak inspiratory pressure is 45 cm H2O. His initial arterial blood gas reveals: pH of 7.49; pO2 160 mmHg; pCO2 35 mmHg The most important initial ventilatory adjustment is to decrease the
options: positive end-expiratory pressure to 5 cm H2O.
respiratory rate to 10 beats per minute.

stem: A 69-year-old man is scheduled to undergo elective myocardial revascularisation. On preoperative physical examination he has a high-pitched, moderately loud right carotid bruit. He denies any neurological symptoms. Duplex ultrasound shows a 50% stenosis of the right internal carotid artery just above the bifurcation of the common carotid artery. Which of the following is the most appropriate plan for the management of this patient?
options: cancel myocardial revascularisation and obtain a carotid angiogram
proceed with carotid artery repair and reschedule myocardial revascularisation
proceed with myocardial revascularisation and follow up with serial Duplex examinations
proceed with simultaneous myocardial revascularisation and carotid artery repair
stage myocardial revascularisation and carotid artery repair

stem: A 64 years old patient with a 2 cm lung cancer, negative lymph nodes on CT staging and diminished pulmonary reserve needs a pulmonary resection. In view of the diminished pulmonary reserve, the decision was taken to perform segmentectomy. Which one of the following statements regarding segmentectomy is correct?
options: equivalent local recurrence rate when compared to lobectomy
fewer pleural space complications when performed without a stapler compared to lobectomy
reduced air leakage when performed with the classic stripping technique compared to lobectomy
reduced mortality compared to lobectomy patients
similar pulmonary function one year after operation compared to lobectomy

stem: Anti-platelet therapy is an important component of medical therapy post coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). While aspirin administration is a Class I indication after CABG, the benefit of concomitant clopidogrel is a controversial issue. Which one of the following statements regarding dual anti-platelet therapy after CABG is correct?
options: Early occlusion rates are similar among patients treated with single therapy or dual anti-platelet therapy.
Single anti-platelet therapy is associated with a significantly increased arterial graft loss compared to dual anti-platelet therapy.
In-hospital or 30-day mortality is lower with dual anti-platelet therapy compared to single anti-platelet therapy alone.
Risk of angina or perioperative myocardial infarction was lower with dual anti-platelet therapy compared to single anti-platelet therapy alone.
Dual anti-platelet therapy is associated with a significantly increased incidence of major bleeding episodes compared to single anti-platelet therapy alone.

stem: The radial artery (RA), as an alternative to the saphenous vein or the right internal thoracic artery (RITA) for coronary artery bypass grafting, has gained considerable interest over the years. Radial Artery Patency Study (RAPS) Investigators sought to determine the relative patency rate of radial-artery and saphenous vein grafts in a randomized trial in which they controlled for bias in the selection of patients and vessels. Which one of the following statements regarding RAPS is correct?
options: The primary endpoint was all-cause death.
Diffuse narrowing of the graft (the angiographic "string sign") was present in 30 percent of radial artery grafts.
At one year similar graft occlusion rates were observed for radial artery and saphenous vein grafts.
At five years the frequency of functional graft occlusion was lower in radial arteries compared with saphenous vein grafts.

stem: The retrotracheal space (also known as the Raider triangle or retrotracheal triangle) is a radiolucent area that extends from the thoracic inlet to the aortic arch and is visible on lateral chest radiographs. A wide spectrum of diseases can occur in this region; they may arise either from the normal contents of the retrotracheal space or from adjacent structures. Which one of the following statements regarding the retrotracheal space is correct?
options: Lungs are a normal content of the retrotracheal space.
The posterior tracheal line forms the posterior margin of the retrotracheal space.
The posterior tracheal line is produced by oesophagus in contact with the posterior wall of the trachea.
The most common lesions in the retrotracheal space are neurogenic in origin.
Right recurrent laryngeal nerve is the most consistent content of the retrotracheal space.

stem: Oesophageal duplication cysts are congenital abnormalities of the oesophagus. Oesophageal duplication cysts
options: account for 25% of all tumours and tumour-like lesions of the oesophagus.
are in the lower part of the oesophagus in approximately 60% of cases.
are lined by gastric mucosa in most cases.
typically manifest as heterogenous spheric or tubular masses in proximity to the oesophageal wall on CT scan.

stem: The treatment of complex pathologies of the aortic arch and proximal descending aorta represents a significant challenge for cardiac surgeons. Various surgical techniques and prostheses have been implemented over the past several decades, all with varying degrees of success. The introduction of the frozen elephant trunk (FET) technique facilitates one-stage repair of such pathologies. Which one of the following statements regarding FET is correct?
options: The reported mortality is in excess of 20%.
Multiple organ failure is the most frequent cause of death.
Spinal cord injury is experienced by 25% of patients.
Cerebral perfusion time strongly correlates with mortality.

stem: Conventional coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) performed with the use of cardiopulmonary bypass is a well-validated treatment for patients with ischemic heart disease. OFF-PUMP coronary artery bypass grafting (OPCAB) has been suggested to reduce the number of perioperative complications, especially in elderly patients. The Danish on-pump versus OFF-PUMP randomization study compares OPCAB with conventional CABG. Which one of the following statements regarding the Danish on-pump versus OFF-PUMP randomization study is correct?
options: The primary endpoint was graft patency.
At the 6-month follow-up, mortality was lower with OPCAB.
Both groups showed significant improvement in self-assessed health-related quality of life.
The trial randomized patients aged ≥ 80 years.
There was no difference between the proportion of open grafts with on-pump CABG and OPCAB.

stem: Off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting compared with coronary revascularization with cardiopulmonary bypass seems safe and results in about the same outcome in low-risk patients. Observational studies indicate that off-pump surgery may provide more benefit in high-risk patients. The best bypass surgery trial conducted was to compare 30-day outcomes in high-risk patients randomized to coronary artery bypass grafting without or with cardiopulmonary bypass. Which one of the following statements regarding the best bypass surgery trial is correct?
options: The primary outcome was all-cause mortality.
Fewer grafts per patient were performed in the off-pump group.
No significant differences in the composite primary outcome were found at 30-day follow-up.
Fewer strokes were experienced by the off-pump group.
More acute myocardial infarctions were experienced by the off-pump group.

stem: The Medtronic Freestyle bioprosthesis (FSB) provides an alternative to other prostheses for both aortic valve and aortic root surgery. FSB compared to homografts
options: is associated with significantly increased hospital mortality.
is associated with comparable reduction in left ventricular mass index.
is associated with superior reduction in left ventricular mass index.

stem: Bronchopulmonary sequestration, intralobar and extralobar, represents an anomaly of tracheobronchial branching with retention of the embryonic systemic arterial supply. Which one of the following statements regarding bronchopulmonary sequestration is correct?
options: Extralobar sequestration is much more common.
Intralobar sequestration is characterised by the sequestered lung having its own separate pleural covering.
Extralobar sequestration usually is found on the right side next to the hemidiaphragm.
Extralobar sequestration usually is diagnosed later in adulthood compared to intralobar sequestration.
Multiple supply arteries are found in 15% of sequestrations.
